html:
Gule Wamkulu, the great dance, is the masked dancing of the Nyau secret society of the Chewa people of Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique, performed at funerals, initiations and memorials.

Dancers wearing masks of wood and straw, often representing spirits of the dead, animals and stock characters, perform in a trance-like state, and are believed to be spirits rather than men. Initiation into the society is part of a boy's coming of age.

Christian missions tried to suppress it, and it became a sign of Chewa resistance. Under Hastings Banda it was used at state events. UNESCO listed it in 2005. It is one of the oldest living institutions of the Maravi world in Malawi.
sum: Gule Wamkulu, the great dance, is the masked dancing of the Nyau secret society of the Chewa people of Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique, performed at funerals, initiations and memorials.
